result.topic_en: Latin text from Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, concluding the case where the solution u depends on time and only two variables, and posing the question of when the quadratic form Σ b_{ι,ι'} ds_ι ds_{ι'} can be transformed into a given form Σ a_{ι,ι'} dx_ι dx_{ι'}.
result.transcription:
12.
functio ipsius $\alpha$, siquidem $\lambda$ et $\mu$ sunt inaequales. Ergo $p$ et $q$ vice variabilium independentium fungi possunt. Praeterea ex aequatione $\lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ invenitur $s = $ const.
In hoc igitur casu $u$ aut est functio ipsius $t$ et unius tantum variabilis, aut alteram utram formarum
$\alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + $ [-const-] const. $\quad (\alpha + \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + $ const.
induet, valore $\mu = 0$ non excluso.

Postquam formae quas functio $u$ induere potest inventae sunt, aequationes $F_\iota = 0$, quas brevitati consulentes perscribere noluimus, facillimae sunt formatu. Unde in singulis quibusque casibus et forma
$\begin{pmatrix} b_{1,1}, & b_{2,2}, & b_{3,3} \\ b_{2,3}, & b_{3,1}, & b_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$
et forma adjuncta
$\begin{pmatrix} \beta_{1,1} & \beta_{2,2} & \beta_{3,3} \\ \beta_{2,3} & \beta_{3,1} & \beta_{1,2} \end{pmatrix}$
innotescit. Si jam in expressionibus $\sum \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in locos quantitatum $s_1, s_2, s_3$ functiones quaelibet ipsarum $x_1, x_2, x_3$ substituantur, manifesto obtinebuntur casus omnes, in quibus $u$ functio temporis et duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit. Unde quaestio prior soluta erit.

Superest ut quaeramus, quando expressio $\sum \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam $\sum a_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$ transformari possit.

methods.what: From the equation λu = ∂u/∂t it follows that s is constant
methods.quote: ex aequatione $\lambda u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ invenitur $s = $ const.

methods.what: Classification: u is either a function of t and one variable, or has one of two exponential forms in t
methods.quote: $\alpha e^{\lambda t} + \beta e^{\mu t} + $ [-const-] const. $\quad (\alpha + \beta t) e^{\lambda t} + $ const.

methods.what: All cases where u depends on time and two variables are obtained by substituting arbitrary functions of x_1,x_2,x_3 for s_1,s_2,s_3 in the quadratic differential form
methods.quote: Si jam in expressionibus $\sum \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in locos quantitatum $s_1, s_2, s_3$ functiones quaelibet ipsarum $x_1, x_2, x_3$ substituantur, manifesto obtinebuntur casus omnes, in quibus $u$ functio temporis et duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit.

items.english: Hence the first question will be solved.

items.quote: Superest ut quaeramus, quando expressio $\sum \beta_{\iota,\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam $\sum a_{\iota,\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$ transformari possit.
items.english: It remains for us to inquire when the expression Σ β_{ι,ι'} ds_ι ds_{ι'} can be transformed into the given form Σ a_{ι,ι'} dx_ι dx_{ι'}.
